roadmap_phase: Phase 2 - Agent Launcher MVP / Supervisor Loop
purpose: Define the minimal SAFE MCP supervisor loop contract for Codex-managed worker pickup/review/result reporting: Codex -> MCP -> worker CLI -> MCP -> Codex. This artifact is design/schema ONLY. It adds no server wiring, no subprocess/exec/fork/shell/network code, and it patches NO source file. It does not enable real process launch and does not mutate any task status; every task-status write stays behind the pre-existing AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES gate plus (for task_mcp-topic runners) the B06 PER_WAVE_RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST prefix check, both entirely unchanged by this task.
no_source_patch_marker: This task's allowed_writes contains zero paths under tools/aiworkhub/src/. No .py file is created or modified by this task. tools/aiworkhub is a nested git repo shared with other concurrent workers; any dirty src/ files observed at task time belong to OTHER in-flight tasks, not this one.
flow_overview: One supervised loop = 4 legs, always starting and ending at Codex. Codex requests a dispatch (leg 1); the MCP server would hand an argv template to a worker CLI process (leg 2, NEVER executed under this or any current contract); the worker CLI would report completion back to the MCP server (leg 3, unreachable in dryrun-only mode because no worker is ever really launched); and Codex polls status and performs the real finalization via taskctl OUTSIDE this MCP boundary (leg 4). Only legs 1 and 4 are ever exercised for real today; legs 2 and 3 are schema-reserved for the future gated launch executor.

flow_legs.name: codex_to_mcp_dispatch_request

mode.note: a 'live' value is rejected with launch_blocked_disabled, never silently promoted

supervisor_request_id.description: NEW in B07: caller-supplied or server-generated correlation id tying together all 4 legs of ONE supervised loop; opaque, not persisted to any new store
NEW in B07: echoes/generates the correlation id from the request

supervisor_state.description: NEW in B07: planned if decision==launch_planned and no audit entry yet written; dispatched_dryrun once the audit entry is appended; blocked on any precondition failure

error.description: NEW in B07: populated only when supervisor_state==blocked

flow_legs.lifecycle_transition: null -> planned -> dispatched_dryrun (or -> blocked on precondition failure)
flow_legs.causer: mcp_server (audit-log write only; never a task_status mutation)

flow_legs.name: mcp_to_worker_cli_argv_handoff
flow_legs.mechanism: NOT an MCP round-trip and NOT executed by this or any current task. would_run_argv from leg 1's response is an argv-list TEMPLATE only (per agent_launcher_mvp_b02_v1.invariant.launch_implemented=false / phase2_orchestration_contract_b104_v1.invariant.launch_code_added=false). This contract adds no subprocess/exec/fork/shell/network code.
flow_legs.existing_worker_protocol_reused: The real worker loop that already exists and that THIS Claude worker session is itself running right now: python3 AITools/taskctl.py auto-pickup/brief/show/stage/guard-staged/review. A future gated launch executor would spawn exactly this CLI loop; this contract does not change it.
flow_legs.causer: external / out-of-band: the worker itself running `taskctl review <task_id>`. The MCP layer NEVER causes this transition -- it only later OBSERVES it (leg 4).

flow_legs.name: worker_cli_to_mcp_result_report

supervisor_request_id.description: NEW in B07: correlates back to leg 1

supervisor_state.const_reachable_value_in_dryrun: worker_review_ready is reported here only as an OBSERVATION of leg-2's external transition, never CAUSED by this call

flow_legs.reality_in_this_contract: Always returns verdict=not_applicable_mvp or pending because no worker process was ever really launched by MCP (leg 2 is never executed). A real worker's own `taskctl review` call is the true signal; it is observed via leg 4 (aiworkhub_agent_task_status), not created by this tool.
flow_legs.lifecycle_transition: worker_review_ready (report only; no MCP-caused state change)
flow_legs.causer: none (read-only observation of an already-external transition)

flow_legs.name: mcp_to_codex_status_and_handoff

taskctl_status.description: verbatim core.show_task(task_id) / taskctl show <task_id> result; taskctl JSONL/SQLite remains sole source of truth

supervisor_state.description: NEW in B07: derived read-only from taskctl_status via the SAME classifier core._lifecycle_state already implements (finished/blocked/review/processing/pending), mapped onto the supervisor vocabulary; never written back

flow_legs.codex_action_after_receiving: python3 AITools/taskctl.py review <task_id> --runner <runner> (worker-side, already happened) followed by python3 AITools/taskctl.py done <task_id> (Codex-side finalize) -- both REAL, EXISTING, gated commands entirely OUTSIDE this MCP contract's scope.
flow_legs.lifecycle_transition: worker_review_ready -> codex_reviewed (Codex has examined the report) -> [external `taskctl done` -> task finished; tracked by taskctl/taskdb, not by this contract]
flow_legs.causer: codex, via the pre-existing taskctl CLI, never via a new MCP write path

planned.description: A dispatch request has been validated against all preconditions (runner/topic allowlist, no collision, no missing artifact) but no audit entry has been written yet.

dispatched_dryrun.description: The dispatch plan's audit entry has been appended (decision=launch_planned, launch_enabled=false, launch_implemented=false). This is the ceiling state actually reachable end-to-end by this contract; nothing beyond this is ever really launched.

worker_review_ready.description: The task card's OWN canonical status/worker_status (owned by AITools/taskdb.py) shows review/ready_for_review/awaiting_review because a worker independently ran `taskctl review <task_id>`.
worker_review_ready.who_causes_entry: external worker via the pre-existing taskctl CLI; MCP only observes via leg 3/4

codex_reviewed.description: Codex has read a worker_review_ready task's status/result report (leg 4) and made a finalization decision. Reaching this state records no new field on the task card itself; it is purely the supervisor's own bookkeeping that Codex has looked at the report.
codex_reviewed.who_causes_entry: codex, via leg 4 read + its own out-of-band review of the report

blocked.description: Any error-taxonomy condition halted progression. Reachable from any other state. Never partially mutates the task card.
blocked.who_causes_entry: mcp_server, on precondition/error detection at any leg

lifecycle_transitions.trigger: audit entry appended for the plan
external: worker runs `taskctl review <task_id>` on its own
codex reads leg-4 status and examines the report
error_taxonomy match at leg 1 (collision | runner_topic_mismatch | missing_artifact)

lifecycle_invariant: These 5 states describe the SUPERVISOR REQUEST's own tracked progress through the loop -- entirely distinct from, and read-only with respect to, the task card's own canonical status/worker_status fields owned exclusively by AITools/taskdb.py and mutated exclusively by AITools/taskctl.py's existing write commands. No tool in this contract writes task_status, worker_status, or any queue row. 'No writes unless explicit future gate' means even the currently-existing gated writes (auto-pickup/review/start/done/usage/export-jsonl) stay behind the pre-existing AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES gate (default '0') and, for task_mcp-topic runners, the B06 PER_WAVE_RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST prefix check -- both entirely unchanged by this task.

no_credential_read.detail: This contract adds no code that reads credential/secret env values or files. It reuses core.py's existing _sanitize_env_for_audit() pattern conceptually: only env var NAMES + set/unset booleans may ever be logged, never values.

no_daemon_start.detail: No new long-running process, listener, or background loop is introduced. The MCP server remains the existing stdio request/response FastMCP process; this contract adds no additional daemon and no new server entrypoint.

no_real_process_launch.detail: Mirrors agent_launcher_mvp_b02_v1 and phase2_orchestration_contract_b104_v1 invariants exactly: launch_implemented=false, launch_enabled_by_default=false, shell_invocation=false, real_agent_spawn_used=false. Leg 2 is a would_run_argv template only, never executed.

no_writes_unless_explicit_future_gate.detail: Every task-status-mutating action stays behind the EXISTING AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES gate (default '0') plus, for task_mcp-topic runners, the B06 PER_WAVE_RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST prefix check (core.check_runner_topic_allowlist). This contract adds zero new write paths and does not touch writes_allowed(), WRITE_COMMANDS, RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST, or PER_WAVE_RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST.

collision.trigger: Two or more active task cards (pending/processing/review/blocked) declare overlapping allowed_writes paths, so a dispatch would collide with another in-flight card.
collision.detection_point: leg 1 preflight, reusing python3 AITools/taskctl.py collision-guard (scripts/build_tasking_parallel_group_collision_guard_v1.scan_collisions) -- the same mechanism as phase2_orchestration_contract_b104_v1.launch_preconditions.collision_guard_preflight, unchanged by this task.
collision.result: supervisor_state -> blocked; no dispatch audit entry recorded; task card untouched.

stale_task.trigger: The supervisor's cached view of a task card (from an earlier taskctl show/export read) no longer matches the LIVE card when re-checked -- e.g. worker_status flips from unclaimed to claimed by a concurrent runner, or status regresses/advances unexpectedly between reads. This is the same shared-queue TOCTOU race already documented for parallel workers.
stale_task.detection_point: leg 1 preflight re-read and leg 4 status re-read, comparing against the previously observed snapshot.
stale_task.result: supervisor_state -> blocked; Codex must re-run aiworkhub_agent_task_status (leg 4) before retrying leg 1.

runner_topic_mismatch.trigger: The (runner, topic, action) triple fails core.check_runner_topic_allowlist -- unknown pair, malformed token, or action not permitted for that runner/topic.
runner_topic_mismatch.detection_point: leg 1, reusing core.check_runner_topic_allowlist (RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST + B06 PER_WAVE_RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST + CODEX_RUNNER wildcard), entirely unchanged by this task.
runner_topic_mismatch.example_reason: one of: unknown_runner_topic_pair | malformed_runner:invalid_characters | malformed_topic:invalid_characters | action_not_allowed_for_runner_topic:<action> | per_wave_action_not_allowed:<action> | codex_action_not_allowed:<action>
runner_topic_mismatch.result: supervisor_state -> blocked; mirrors the existing returncode-126 blocked-write semantics of core.run_taskctl.

missing_artifact.trigger: A path listed in the task card's read_first or allowed_writes does not exist on disk when the supervisor preflights it (e.g. a read_first file was renamed or never landed).
missing_artifact.detection_point: leg 1 preflight: a pure filesystem existence check over read_first (and, before leg 3/4 acceptance, allowed_writes).

failed_validation.trigger: One of the task card's validation commands would exit nonzero when run by the worker.
failed_validation.detection_point: leg 3/4 -- reported verdict from the worker or, in dryrun-only mode, always verdict=not_applicable_mvp, so this branch is schema-reserved and NOT exercised end-to-end by this task (no real worker is ever launched to fail validation).
failed_validation.result: supervisor_state -> blocked; codex_reviewed is never reached for that supervisor_request_id until re-dispatched.

taskctl_status.note: verbatim taskctl show T1 stdout, not reproduced here

response.summary: No process was ever launched for this task; nothing to collect. worker_review_ready (if present) reflects an external taskctl review call, not this tool.

neural_bridge_note.doctrine: Per AIWorkHub neural-control-first doctrine, adapter/runner/topic SELECTION for a real future launch must be a LEARNED routing + abstain decision, never a regex/keyword cue router. This contract adds NO cue router: the lifecycle state machine and error taxonomy are static, human-authored safety/interface boundaries (a request/response shape plus a deterministic classifier reused from core._lifecycle_state), not a cognitive routing decision. Intelligence over which task/adapter/runner to dispatch remains deferred to the tracked migration below.

no_launch_code_marker: This artifact defines JSON schema only. No subprocess/exec/fork/shell/network code is introduced by this task. Real launch code remains gated behind the future CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_GATED_LAUNCH_EXECUTOR task and every launch_precondition already listed in phase2_orchestration_contract_b104_v1.

rollback.action: Delete the 4 new artifact files introduced by this task (this contract, its eval, its next_wave proposal, its test). Nothing outside tools/aiworkhub/{contracts,eval,data/tasking,tests} references them, and no source file was changed, so rollback is a pure file removal with zero code dependency and zero data migration.

any error_taxonomy category is dropped below 5
